children: New Delhi, Nov. 16 -- Shares of Inox Wind Limited fell nearly 9.17% during Monday's intraday trading session, days after the announcement of the second quarter result for the financial year 2026-27. Monday's decline has come as the renewable energy stock has fallen 60% in one year.

The recent decline has come after Inox Wind reported lower-than expected profit numbers for Q2FY26. The company's EBITDA margin came lower as it was impacted by commodity/raw material inflation and supply chain cost headwinds. The brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited (MOFSL), in its latest report, also reduced Inox Wind share price target, but keep the rating unchanged.

Inox Wind's consolidated revenue came 7% above estimates, while EBITDA was 5% below expectations, according to MOFSL, lower EBITDA margin was due to commodity/raw material inflation and supply chain cost headwinds.
"We lower our FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates by 21%/14%, factoring in lower estimated deliveries and moderated EBITDA margins of 18%/19% (vs. management guidance of 20%)," read the brokerage report.

Motilal Oswal maintained a 'Buy' rating for the stock with a target price of Rs.74 per share. "We reiterate our BUY rating, given attractive valuations, with a revised TP of INR74 per share (based on 20x FY28E EPS)."

Inox Wind reported a 42% annual decline in its consolidated net profit to Rs.69 crore in the September quarter due to higher expenses. Its total income also surged to Rs.1,378 crore in the quarter from Rs.1,162 crore a year ago. Its total expense rose to Rs.1,275 crore in the quarter from Rs.993 crore in the same period a year ago.

The stock was trading 9.34% higher at Rs.58.55 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.10,118.83 crore at 10:23 am on Monday, November 16. Its share price value declined 12.22% in one week. Its share price value has dropped by 20.69% in three months, 60% in one year, and 68.76% in two years.
